subject: Copied-client S5 second-sandbag probe stops early at dry-bank route waypoint 4; delayed accepted Move changes the interpretation
scope: One isolated original-client 1.16.5.0 run with ordinary copied Game DLL and archived post-Conrad-corpse character DB. Only the copied objective 1995/1 timer anchor was reset. The planned screen-right second-sandbag probe was not reached.

observations.finding: The copied client reached dry-bank route waypoint 4 after the accepted position (-127.87109,83.375,30.285156), aiming for (-135.742,84.769,30.594). The first accepted spatial Move after a forward hold was (-128.15234,83.85156,27.289062), 0.40 m farther from that waypoint. The driver treated this as divergence and ended before the second sandbag.
observations.source_location: driver-second-sandbag.log final 13 lines; positions.tsv rows with timestamps 1790279792681 and 1790279793182

observations.finding: The trace then received a stationary accepted packet followed by (-129.77344,84.16016,27.363281) at timestamp 1790279798381, while the driver was already stopped. Relative to the pre-hold point, this delayed packet had moved about 1.09 m closer to the waypoint, reversing the first-packet conclusion. The screenshot after driver exit shows the route rock and wreckage with full health and about 00:06:50 on the reset timer.
Mission 1995 was still state 0; objective 1 active and objectives 2 and 3 complete. SQLite integrity was ok. No second-sandbag position, bomb prompt or bomb interaction was reached in this run.

assessment.finding: A single first post-hold Move packet with poor target progress can precede delayed movement toward the waypoint. The early divergence guard was too strict for this client/telemetry timing. It remains unknown whether this delayed movement would have safely completed the dry-bank route; the archive does not test the second sandbag or bomb. A future isolated driver should wait a bounded interval for positive target progress across all fresh accepted packets, while still stopping on sustained wrong-way movement, unsafe elevation, health loss or timer expiry.
